ack_mode.description: delivered: an event is acked once a subscriber's connection took it; while nobody does, it waits (unacked, so the rest wait in the node's queue, durable if it is). buffered: once it's in the channel's replay ring (faster; with nobody subscribed it's only kept for replay).
ack_mode.title: Ack

allowed_channels.description: The channel names events and subscribers may use, as patterns (* within a /-separated segment, ** across). Empty: any name.
allowed_channels.title: Allowed channels

allowed_origins.description: The Origins browsers may connect from, or ["*"]; empty: any. Clients without an Origin (not browsers) aren't affected.
allowed_origins.title: Allowed origins

auth.description: none, bearer (Authorization: Bearer <token>), api_key (a header or query parameter) or mtls (client certificates).
auth.title: Authentication

auth_secrets.description: bearer and api_key: {"label": "secret"}. The label of the one a request used becomes its event's principal.
auth_secrets.title: Tokens / keys

base_path.description: A prefix for the route: <base>/ws/{channel} (?after=<id> resumes from the replay ring).
base_path.title: Base path

default_channel.description: The channel of events without one.
default_channel.title: Default channel

delivery_timeout_ms.description: delivered: how long an event waits for a subscriber before it's refused (retryable: the hub delivers it again, up to the node's delivery.max_attempts). 0: as long as it takes.
delivery_timeout_ms.title: Delivery timeout (ms)

frame.description: How an event becomes a message: auto (text if the data is UTF-8, else binary), text, binary, or envelope: JSON text {id, event, content_type, data, encoding?}, with {"type": "gap", "missed"} markers, so clients can resume (?after=<id>) and see what they missed.
frame.title: Messages

h2c.description: Without TLS: accept HTTP/2 with prior knowledge besides HTTP/1.1.
h2c.title: Cleartext HTTP/2

header_allowlist.description: The only request headers events carry (wins over the denylist).
header_allowlist.title: Header allowlist

header_denylist.description: Request headers events never carry. Default: authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key (and the API key's header).
header_denylist.title: Header denylist

h2_max_send_buf_bytes.description: HTTP/2: what one stream may have waiting to be sent before its writer waits. Memory per stream with slow readers (e.g. SSE subscribers): with 1 000 HTTP/2 SSE subscribers, 4 KiB gave ~3x the throughput and a fifth of the memory of 64 KiB, at ~10 % less for a single fast stream.

listen.description: Address and port. Anything but loopback needs auth (or auth: none set explicitly).
listen.title: Listen on

max_client_message_bytes.description: Client messages are ignored; larger ones close the connection (1009).
max_client_message_bytes.title: Largest client message

max_in_flight.description: Events handled at once (with ack_mode delivered: waiting for a subscriber at once); the hub holds the rest.
max_in_flight.title: Events in flight

max_subscribers.description: In all (waiting long polls included); more are refused with 503.
max_subscribers.title: Max subscribers

mtls_allow.description: mtls: SHA-256 fingerprints or names (SAN DNS / URI, or CN). Empty: any certificate the client CA signed.
mtls_allow.title: Allowed client certificates

ping_interval_s.description: The server pings each client this often; a client that has sent nothing since the last ping is closed.
ping_interval_s.title: Ping interval (s)

read_buffer_bytes.description: Per connection, allocated up front: clients only send pings and closes here, so a small one saves memory with many clients.
read_buffer_bytes.title: Read buffer (bytes)

replay_bytes.description: Bytes of data kept per channel; a larger event is refused.
replay_bytes.title: Replay bytes

replay_events.description: Events kept per channel, for subscribers resuming from an id and for slow readers.
replay_events.title: Replay events

slow_policy.description: A subscriber that falls behind the replay ring: disconnect it, or skip it ahead to the oldest kept event after a gap marker.
slow_policy.title: Slow subscribers

subprotocols.description: The subprotocols the server speaks (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol), in order of preference.
subprotocols.title: Subprotocols

tls_cert.description: Uploaded PEM file: the server's certificate chain. Turns TLS on (HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 by ALPN).
tls_cert.title: TLS certificate

tls_client_auth.description: With a client CA: optional or required (required for auth: mtls).
tls_client_auth.title: Client certificates

tls_client_ca.description: Uploaded PEM file: the CA(s) of client certificates (mTLS).
tls_client_ca.title: Client CA

tls_key.description: Uploaded PEM file: the server's private key.
tls_key.title: TLS key

write_buffer_bytes.description: Per connection: how much is gathered before a write. It grows to fit a larger message (and stays that large for the connection), so large events cost memory per client whatever this is; 0 writes each message at once.
write_buffer_bytes.title: Write buffer (bytes)

write_timeout_ms.description: A message not written within this long (a stuck client) closes the connection.
write_timeout_ms.title: Write timeout (ms)
